info.title: Bitbybit CAD Cloud API
info.description: High-performance parametric CAD model generation API. Supports multi-format output (STEP, GLTF, decomposed mesh), pipeline execution, file-based conversion, and async job processing.

get.description: Returns the operational status of the Bitbybit CAD Cloud API, including service health and readiness. Requires no authentication, so it is suitable for uptime monitoring, load balancer probes and deployment smoke tests.

post.description: Runs a single CAD operation by its fully-qualified identifier.
Runs multiple operations sequentially. Use '$ref:N' in params to reference step N's result.

Runs several independent CAD operations in parallel as one compound task. Each sub-operation is executed on its own and produces its own downloadable result, so use this when the operations do not depend on each other - for a sequence where each step consumes the previous one's output, use the chained pipeline endpoint instead. Returns 202 with a compound task id; poll it and download the per-sub-task manifest when it completes.

get.description: Lists every parametric model available for generation, by name. Use the returned names with the definitions and generation endpoints to discover each model's parameter schema and defaults before submitting a job.

post.description: Returns parameter schemas and defaults for the requested model names.
Generic endpoint - works for any registered model. See model-specific endpoints for fully typed parameters. Always returns 202 with a task ID for polling.
Creates a compound task with one sub-task per item. Each item can have different parameters but shares the same output config.

get.description: Returns parameter schema, types, defaults, and limits for the specified model.

post.description: Parametric dragon-scale textured cup with twisted lofted body, voronoi-like skin cells, and configurable shell thickness. All parameters are optional - defaults produce a ready-to-print model.

Parametric 3D-printable desktop phone holder/stand with a lofted cradle surface, optional ornamental perforations, and a phone mock-up shape. All parameters are optional - defaults produce a ready-to-print model.
Simple STEP → glTF conversion using a previously uploaded file. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Convert - STEP to glTF (.glb), advanced options
post.description: Full-control STEP → glTF conversion with fine-grained mesh, export, and coordinate options. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.
STEP → glTF conversion with Draco geometry compression using a previously uploaded file. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Convert - STEP to Draco-compressed glTF (.glb), advanced options
post.description: Full-control STEP → glTF conversion with Draco geometry compression. Combines fine-grained mesh, export, and coordinate options with Draco quantization controls. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold a face to flat geometry
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold: flattens a single developable face (by index) of an uploaded STEP shape. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the flattened geometry is delivered as the task's output files.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold a face, metrics report
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal analysis: computes the unfold metrics report (developability, area, ...) for a single face of an uploaded STEP shape. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the JSON report is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids to flat geometry
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold: loads every solid in an uploaded STEP file and flattens each to a flat pattern. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; every flat is one part of a single output per format, named after its solid, so a nesting call reads one part per flat.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids, metrics report
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal analysis: computes per-solid unfold metrics for every solid in an uploaded STEP file. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the JSON report array is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids, geometry + report
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold, full workflow: flattens every solid in an uploaded STEP file AND returns per-solid metrics in one call. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; every flat is one part of a single output per format, named after its solid, and the per-solid report array is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids and nest the flats on sheets
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold and true-shape nesting in one call: flattens every solid in an uploaded STEP file and nests the flat patterns on sheets straight away, without writing them to a file and reading them back. Left out, the sheets are sized for the flats and the spacing and margin are scaled to them; 'fileUnit' reads a file whose header names the wrong unit. Every length is in millimetres. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the nested sheets come in the requested formats as on POST /api/v1/cad/pro/nesting/nest, 'flat-meshes' gives each solid's flat triangulated where it was unfolded, the NestingReport (each part naming its solid) is the metadata result, and the per-solid unfold report array is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Nesting - place flat parts on sheets or a strip
post.description: Proprietary true-shape 2D nesting: places the flat parts of uploaded STEP files onto rectangular sheets or one strip, turning and flipping them as each part's options allow, with a spacing that holds on the true curved edges and parts placed inside other parts' holes. Every part a file places is a part, with each of its solids on its own, so an unfold's output gives one part per flat pattern; 'stepFileIds' gives the full rule. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; every used sheet is one compound of its placed parts, laid in a row on the XZ plane, combined into one output per format, and the NestingReport (placements with their transforms, each part as read, what was left and why, totals) is delivered as the metadata result.

post.summary: Nesting - read parts without nesting them
post.description: Reads the parts of uploaded STEP files as nesting would and reports each one's file, kind, outline size, area and cut length, or why it cannot be nested. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the NestingInspection is delivered as the metadata result.
Returns a pre-signed URL for uploading a file via PUT.

200.description: The same bytes were uploaded and confirmed under this key before (matched by sha256): the existing confirmed file, ready to reference. No PUT is needed.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the files uploaded under your API key, newest first, with each file's id, original name, size, upload status and expiry. Use it to find the file id to pass to a conversion endpoint, and to check that an upload through a pre-signed URL actually completed before you reference it.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Defaults to the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many files to return per page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only files in this upload state: pending (a pre-signed URL was issued but the upload has not been confirmed), confirmed (the blob is stored and usable), or expired.

get.description: Returns metadata and download URL for a single file.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an uploaded file and the stored blob behind it. This cannot be undone, and any task result that still points at the blob stops resolving. Files also expire on their own, so call this only when you need the storage released sooner than that.

post.description: Confirms that the file was successfully uploaded to the pre-signed URL.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of your tasks, newest first, each with its id, kind, status, creation time and result link when finished. Filter by status to poll only what is still running, or by kind to separate model generation, STEP conversion, pipelines and compound runs. This is the endpoint to build a job dashboard on rather than polling every task id individually.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Defaults to the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many tasks to return per page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only tasks in this state. waiting and queued are not started yet, processing is running, completed has a downloadable result, failed carries an error, cancelled was stopped by you, and expired means the result has been cleaned up.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Return only tasks of this kind: cad for a single operation, model for a registered parametric model, convert-simple and convert-advanced for STEP conversions, pipeline for a chained run, compound for a parallel run.

get.description: Returns the current status and metadata of a task.

delete.description: Cancels a waiting or queued task. Has no effect on completed/failed tasks.

get.description: Returns a download URL for the task's primary result. For compound tasks, returns a manifest with per-sub-task download links.

200.description: Result download link (standard) or compound manifest

get.summary: Tasks - get result in a specific format
get.description: Returns a download URL for the requested output format (e.g. glb, step, stpz).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Result format (e.g. glb, step, stpz, metadata, decomposed-mesh)

get.description: Returns download URLs for every available result format in a single call. Use this instead of making multiple requests to /result/{format}.

200.description: Download links for all available formats

post.summary: Tasks - retry a failed or cancelled task
post.description: Re-queues a failed or cancelled task with the same parameters.

409.description: Task is not in a retryable state

operation.description: Fully-qualified CAD operation identifier (e.g. 'occt.shapes.solid.createBox', 'manifold.primitives.cube', 'jscad.booleans.union'). Supports OCCT, Manifold, JSCAD, and vector/math operations.

params.description: Operation-specific parameters - varies by operation. See model definitions for available parameters.

ExecuteBody.description: Execute a single Bitbybit CAD operation. The operation runs asynchronously and returns a task ID for polling.

steps.description: Ordered list of CAD operations executed sequentially. Later steps can reference earlier results using '$ref:N' syntax. Supports map and choice control-flow steps.

inputFiles.description: References to previously uploaded files. Use '$file:N' in step params to inject file contents (optionally '$file:N:<format>:<codec>' to pick a read format and/or decompress - see PipelineStep.params).

outputs.description: Output format options applied to the final pipeline result. Supports json, csv, stl, 3mf in addition to standard formats. If omitted, raw result data is stored.

PipelineBody.description: Execute a chain of Bitbybit CAD operations sequentially. Supports $ref:N step references, $file:N file inputs, map iteration, and choice conditionals.

PipelineAnyStep.description: A pipeline step - either a plain operation, a map (iteration), or a choice (conditional).

type.description: Declares this step as a map (iteration) step

items.description: Source array to iterate over. Typically a '$ref:N' reference to a previous step that produced an array.

steps.description: Sub-steps to execute for each item. Use '$item' for the current element, '$index' for the iteration number.

reduce.description: Optional sub-steps to combine map results. Use '$mapResult' to reference the collected array of iteration outputs.

MapStep.description: Iterate over an array, executing sub-steps for each element. Produces an array of results (or a reduced value).

operation.description: Fully-qualified CAD operation identifier (e.g. 'occt.shapes.solid.createSphere'). Supports OCCT, Manifold, JSCAD, and vector/math operations.

params.description: Operation parameters. Use '$ref:N' (e.g. '$ref:0') to reference the output of a previous step by its zero-based index. Use '$file:N[:<format>][:<codec>]' to reference an input file's contents - <format> is one of text|buffer|uint8|json|base64 (default text), and the optional <codec> is one of raw|gunzip|auto (default raw) to decompress the file first; 'auto' gunzips only when gzip magic bytes are present, so '$file:0:text:auto' reads both plain and gzip-compressed uploads (e.g. .step and .stpz).

output.description: When true, this step's result is included in a separate result.json output alongside any shape files.

PipelineStep.description: A single step in a sequential CAD pipeline. Steps can reference outputs of earlier steps via $ref or input files via $file.

type.description: Declares this step as a choice (conditional) step

value.description: Value to compare. Typically a '$ref:N' reference to a previous step result.

operator.description: Comparison operator to apply between value and compareTo

compareTo.description: Value to compare against. Not required for 'exists' operator.

then.description: Sub-steps to execute when condition is true

else.description: Sub-steps to execute when condition is false. If omitted, produces null.

ChoiceStep.description: Conditional execution - evaluate a condition and run the matching branch.

ComparisonOperator.description: Comparison operator: 'eq' (equal), 'neq' (not equal), 'gt' (greater than), 'gte' (greater or equal), 'lt' (less than), 'lte' (less or equal), 'exists' (value is not null/undefined).

fileId.description: ID of a previously uploaded file (from POST /files/upload)

InputFileItem.description: Reference to an uploaded file to be used as input

formats.description: Output formats to generate. Supports standard CAD formats (step, stpz, gltf, decomposed-mesh) plus pipeline-specific formats (json, csv, stl, 3mf, brep, brep-binary).

meshPrecision.description: Tessellation precision for mesh-based outputs (decomposed-mesh and gltf). Lower values produce denser meshes.

gltfMeshPrecision.description: Override tessellation precision specifically for glTF output. When set, takes precedence over meshPrecision for glTF only.

adjustYtoZ.description: Turns a decomposed-mesh output from Y-up, as the server models, to Z-up. It applies to decomposed-mesh only: a STEP output is always written Z-up, so a STEP sent in comes back as it went in, a glTF output is always Y-up, as glTF asks, and a BREP output keeps the frame the shapes were modelled in, as occt.io.loadBrep reads it back.

includePipelineInMetadata.description: Include the full pipeline definition in metadata.json. Defaults to true. Set to false to exclude it for smaller metadata.

unit.description: The unit the pipeline's shapes are modelled in. Given, a STEP output is written at its true size in millimetres, so CAD tools open the shapes at the right size, and a glTF output is written in metres, the unit glTF viewers assume. Left out, the numbers are written as they are: STEP takes them as millimetres and glTF holds them unscaled. The other formats carry no unit and always hold the numbers as they are. A design build's documents state their own unit, and a unit given here must be the same.

PipelineOutputOptions.description: Controls which output formats are generated for pipeline results. Supports additional formats (json, csv, stl, 3mf, brep, brep-binary) beyond standard model outputs.

PipelineOutputFormat.description: Pipeline output file format. Includes all standard formats plus: 'json' (JSON data), 'csv' (CSV text), 'stl' (binary STL mesh - Manifold/JSCAD only), '3mf' (3MF mesh package - Manifold/JSCAD only), 'brep' (OpenCascade BREP as text) and 'brep-binary' (OpenCascade binary BREP, the smallest and fastest exact form, which keeps the numbering of faces and edges) - both OCCT only, without triangulation, and both in the frame the pipeline modelled the shape in (Y up), so occt.io.loadBrep and occt.io.loadBrepBinary read them back exactly as they were; a Z-up tool such as FreeCAD shows them lying on their backs, where a 'step' output stands upright.

parallel.description: Must be true - signals that items should be processed concurrently

items.description: List of independent CAD operations to execute in parallel. Each item becomes a sub-task.

CompoundExecuteBody.description: Execute multiple independent Bitbybit CAD operations in parallel. Each item runs as a separate sub-task and can be polled individually.

operation.description: Fully-qualified CAD operation identifier. Supports OCCT, Manifold, JSCAD, and vector/math operations.

inputFiles.description: References to previously uploaded files to be used as inputs for this operation

outputFormats.description: Per-item output format overrides. If omitted, the task produces raw result data.

CompoundItem.description: A single operation within a compound (parallel) task. Each item runs independently.

names.description: Array of model slugs to fetch definitions for (e.g. ['dragon-cup', 'phone-nest'])

DefinitionsBody.description: Fetch parameter definitions for one or more parametric models. Returns available parameters, types, defaults, and constraints.

params.description: Model-specific parameters. Omitted params use their defaults. See model definition for available options.

ModelSubmissionBody.description: Submit a parametric model for generation with specified parameters and output formats

formats.description: Output formats to generate. Multiple formats can be requested (e.g. ['gltf', 'stpz']) - each produces a separate downloadable result. Do not include both 'step' and 'stpz' - only one STEP variant is supported per request.

meshPrecision.description: Tessellation precision for mesh-based outputs (decomposed-mesh and gltf). Lower values produce denser meshes. Only ignored when output is limited to step/stpz formats.

gltfMeshPrecision.description: Override tessellation precision specifically for glTF output. When set, takes precedence over meshPrecision for glTF only.

adjustYtoZ.description: Turns a decomposed-mesh output from Y-up, as the server models, to Z-up. It applies to decomposed-mesh only: a STEP output is always written Z-up, so a STEP sent in comes back as it went in, and a glTF output is always Y-up, as glTF asks.

OutputOptions.description: Controls which output formats are generated and their quality settings

OutputFormat.description: Output file format: 'step' (raw STEP), 'stpz' (gzip-compressed STEP), 'decomposed-mesh' (triangulated JSON), 'gltf' (glTF 2.0 binary .glb). Note: 'step' and 'stpz' are mutually exclusive - choose one or the other, not both.

items.description: Array of parameter variations. Each item produces a separate output with the same model.

outputs.description: Output format configuration applied to every item in the batch

BatchModelSubmissionBody.description: Submit multiple parameter variations of the same model for parallel generation

radiusTopOffset.description: How much the top radius differs from bottom

nrSkinCellDivisionsTop.description: Subdivisions at top of each cell

applyOrnaments.description: Add decorative perforations to the surface

fileUnit.description: The unit a STEP file's numbers are really in, when its header states another unit or none: some exporters write a model drawn in metres under a millimetre header. Each file is scaled from it, so the model is read in millimetres, the unit every length of the request and its results is in. A header naming no unit counts as millimetres; a file whose header names a unit other than mm, cm, m or in, or several different ones, is refused, since its unit is converted already. Left out, each file's own unit is used.

UnfoldSolidBody.description: Flatten every constant-thickness sheet-metal solid in an uploaded STEP file AND return the per-solid metrics report - both in one call.

stepFileId.description: ID of the previously uploaded STEP file (returned by the file upload endpoint). Both plain STEP (.step/.stp) and gzip-compressed STEP (.stpz) uploads are accepted - compression is detected automatically.

fileUnit.description: The unit a STEP file's numbers are really in, when its header states another unit or none: some exporters write a model drawn in metres under a millimetre header. Each file is scaled from it, so the model is read in millimetres, the unit every length of the request and its results is in. A header naming no unit counts as millimetres; a file whose header names a unit other than mm, cm, m or in, or several different ones, is refused, since its unit is converted already. Left out, each file's own unit is used.

thicknessOverride.description: Sheet thickness override in millimetres; 0 auto-detects thickness from face pairs.

nesting.description: How the flat patterns are nested. Left out, every flat is placed once on sheets sized for them, turning in quarter turns.

outputs.description: Output formats for the nested sheets and the flat patterns. Defaults to glTF of the nested sheets.

UnfoldAndNestBody.description: Flatten every constant-thickness sheet-metal solid in an uploaded STEP file and nest the flat patterns on sheets in the same call: the per-solid unfold report, the nesting report and the nested sheets, without writing the flats to a file and reading them back.

sheets.description: The stock to nest onto: kinds of rectangular sheets, or one strip. Left out, one kind of sheet is sized for the flat patterns: at least twice as long as it is wide, holding the largest flat with its margins, large enough that all the flats fill about half of it, its sides rounded up. When every flat fits on standard 3000 x 1500 stock and that sheet would be larger, the standard stock is used instead.

quantity.description: How many copies of every flat pattern to place: the number of models to make. Defaults to 1. All copies together, this number times the number of flat patterns, stay within 100000.

allowFlip.description: Whether every flat pattern may be turned over (a half turn about an axis in its plane, never a mirror). Defaults to false.

spacing.description: The least distance kept between any two flat patterns, in millimetres, measured on their true shapes. Defaults to a gap sized to the flats: a fiftieth of the square root of their area, rounded to 1, 2 or 5 of its decade.

margin.description: The band along each sheet's edges that no flat pattern enters, in millimetres. Defaults to the gap sized to the flats, the same one the spacing takes when it is left out; a spacing that is given does not change it.

timeBudgetSeconds.description: How long the nesting may search; the best layout found by then is returned. Defaults to 5 seconds, at most 120.

tolerance.description: How far the straight chords that stand in for curved edges may stray from them, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files); the spacing still holds on the true curves. Defaults to 0.1.

evaluationBudget.description: Stop after this many placements are tried, which makes a run repeatable for one seed; the time budget still applies. 0 means no limit.

seed.description: The seed of the search's random choices. Defaults to 1.

sheetGap.description: The gap between sheets as they are laid out in a row in the output, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files). Defaults to a tenth of the widest sheet.

UnfoldNestingOptions.description: How the flat patterns of an unfold are nested: the stock, the copies, how each flat may turn, and the search settings. Every length is in millimetres.

height.description: The strip's width across, along y, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files). Its length along x is open and is what the nesting makes as short as it can.

cost.description: What the strip costs: one amount, added to the totals' cost whatever length the nesting uses. Defaults to 1.

NestingStrip.description: One strip of open length; it stands alone, never beside other stock.

width.description: The sheet's side along x, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files).

height.description: The sheet's side along y, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files).

quantity.description: How many sheets of this stock there are. Without it, as many as needed.

cost.description: What one sheet of this stock costs. Without costs, the stock that wastes least is opened first (each sheet costs its area).

angles.description: The turns a part may take, in degrees, such as [0, 180] for a grain direction; at most 720.

step.description: Turn in steps of this many degrees; it must divide 360 evenly (90 gives 0, 90, 180 and 270).

NestingRotations.description: How a part may turn on the sheet: a fixed list of angles, steps that divide a full turn, or any angle. Without it a part turns in steps of 90 degrees.

formats.description: Output formats to generate; each gives a separate downloadable result. The nested sheets come in the formats of NestingOutputFormat, and 'flat-meshes' gives each solid's flat pattern triangulated where it was unfolded, tagged with its solidIndex, for showing beside the model; a flat that could not be meshed has no mesh there but is nested all the same, and its unfold report entry says why in 'meshError'. Give 'step' or 'stpz', not both.

meshPrecision.description: Tessellation precision for mesh-based outputs (decomposed-mesh and gltf). Lower values produce denser meshes. Only ignored when output is limited to step/stpz formats.

gltfMeshPrecision.description: Override tessellation precision specifically for glTF output. When set, takes precedence over meshPrecision for glTF only.

adjustYtoZ.description: Turns the decomposed-mesh and flat-meshes outputs from Y-up, as the server models, to Z-up. It applies to those two only: a STEP output is always written Z-up, and a glTF output is always Y-up, as glTF asks.

UnfoldAndNestOutputOptions.description: Which formats the nested sheets and the flat patterns are written in, and their mesh quality.

stepFileIds.description: IDs of previously uploaded STEP files (.step, .stp or gzip-compressed .stpz), at most 50 and 200 MB together. Parts are read file after file, as each file's product structure gives them: every placement of a part (a product) is a part, and a file with no assembly is its one part. Within a part, every solid is a part of its own, in the order they sit, and whatever else it holds stays one part after them (an unfolded flat pattern with its bend lines, a drawing's outline with its holes); a part with no edge is skipped, and a request whose files give no part at all is refused. Parts are read into the Y-up working space the report uses. options.parts[i] pairs with the i-th part over all files, at most 5000, and the report names each part's file.

fileUnit.description: The unit a STEP file's numbers are really in, when its header states another unit or none: some exporters write a model drawn in metres under a millimetre header. Each file is scaled from it, so the model is read in millimetres, the unit every length of the request and its results is in. A header naming no unit counts as millimetres; a file whose header names a unit other than mm, cm, m or in, or several different ones, is refused, since its unit is converted already. Left out, each file's own unit is used.

outputs.description: Output formats for the nested sheets: every used sheet is one part, holding its placed parts and its outline, and all sheets are combined into one output per format. Defaults to glTF.

NestingNestBody.description: Nest the flat parts of uploaded STEP files onto sheets or a strip. A part is a planar face, coplanar faces such as an unfolded sheet-metal part, a plate solid, or a drawing of closed wires; 'stepFileIds' says how parts are read from a file.

sheets.description: The stock to nest onto: kinds of rectangular sheets, or one strip.

parts.description: The options of each part, in the order of the parts; the list may not be longer than the parts there are. A null entry, and every part past the end of the list, takes the defaults. All copies together stay within 100000, every part counting its quantity, or 1 when it has no entry or its entry gives none: the entries given are checked when the request arrives, and the total over every part once the parts are read. The request body may grow by 256 bytes for each of the 5000 parts nesting takes, so the options of every part fit, each with its quantity, a few fixed angles, a flip, a priority and an x direction.

spacing.description: The least distance kept between any two parts, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files), measured on their true shapes. Defaults to 0, where parts that tile exactly may touch.

margin.description: The band along each sheet's edges that no part enters, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files). Defaults to 0.

timeBudgetSeconds.description: How long the search may run; the best layout found by then is returned. Defaults to 10 seconds, at most 120.

tolerance.description: How far the straight chords that stand in for curved edges may stray from them, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files); the spacing still holds on the true curves. Defaults to 0.1.

evaluationBudget.description: Stop after this many placements are tried, which makes a run repeatable for one seed; the time budget still applies. 0 means no limit.

seed.description: The seed of the search's random choices. Defaults to 1.

sheetGap.description: The gap between sheets as they are laid out in a row in the output, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files). Defaults to a tenth of the widest sheet.

NestingOptions.description: The stock, the per-part options and the settings of a nesting run. Every length is in the parts' units: millimetres on the nesting routes, which read their STEP files in millimetres, and the unit a pipeline models its shapes in for an occtPro.nesting step.

quantity.description: How many copies of the part to place. Defaults to 1; 0 leaves the part out.

allowFlip.description: Whether the part may be turned over (a half turn about an axis in its plane, never a mirror). Defaults to false.

priority.description: Parts of higher priority are placed first, so they are the last to be left off when stock runs out. Defaults to 0.

xDirection.description: The direction in the part's plane that a rotation of 0 lays along the sheet's x axis, in the Y-up working space the parts are read into (a STEP file's Z-up numbers are turned a quarter about X first, so the file's +Y is -Z here). A part lying flat keeps its drawn direction without it; one lying askew is squared up to its smallest box.

NestingPartOptions.description: The options of one part, paired with the part of the same index.

formats.description: Output formats to generate; each gives a separate downloadable result. Give 'step' or 'stpz', not both.

meshPrecision.description: Tessellation precision for mesh-based outputs (decomposed-mesh and gltf). Lower values produce denser meshes. Only ignored when output is limited to step/stpz formats.

gltfMeshPrecision.description: Override tessellation precision specifically for glTF output. When set, takes precedence over meshPrecision for glTF only.

adjustYtoZ.description: Turns a decomposed-mesh output from Y-up, as the server models, to Z-up. It applies to decomposed-mesh only: a STEP output is always written Z-up, so a STEP sent in comes back as it went in, and a glTF output is always Y-up, as glTF asks.

NestingOutputOptions.description: Which formats the nested sheets are written in, and their mesh quality.

NestingOutputFormat.description: The formats of the nested sheets: 'step' or 'stpz' (each sheet one part, holding its placed parts and its outline), 'gltf', 'decomposed-mesh' (the placed parts, triangulated), 'dxf' (an AutoCAD 2000 drawing in millimetres: the sheets' outlines on layer SHEETS and the parts' cut paths on layer PARTS, every arc, ellipse and spline exact), 'svg' (the same drawing as an SVG file in millimetres, each layer a group), or 'outlines' (the same cut paths as JSON, each copy in the frame of its sheet and named by its placement, for drawing the layout). A 'dxf' or 'svg' too large to write is left out while every other format is still written, and the task's metadata says why under 'outputsLeftOut' (format to reason); a caveat about a cut file that was written, such as a part whose faces could not be joined into one outline, is given under 'outputNotes' (format to note).

NestingInspectOptions.description: The settings that change how parts are read (tolerance, xDirection); no stock is needed. Every length is in the parts' units: millimetres on the nesting routes, which read their STEP files in millimetres, and the unit a pipeline models its shapes in for an occtPro.nesting step.

filename.description: Original filename including extension (e.g. 'part.step', 'model.obj'). Used for display and format detection.

contentType.description: MIME type of the file (e.g. 'application/step', 'model/gltf-binary'). Must match the actual file content.

bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes. Must match the Content-Length of the subsequent PUT to the upload URL. Maximum: 1 GB.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file content. When provided, enables server-side deduplication - if an identical file was previously uploaded under this API key, the existing file is reused and no upload is needed.

FileUploadBody.description: Request a pre-signed upload URL. After receiving the URL, PUT the raw file bytes to it within the expiration window.

UnfoldReportError.description: Returned when a shape/face cannot be processed by the unfold.

meshError.description: Why the flat pattern has no mesh in the decomposed-mesh or flat-meshes result, when it could not be meshed. The flat is still in every other output and, on unfold-and-nest, in the nest.

UnfoldSolidReportItem.description: Sheet-metal unfold metrics for ONE solid (bend table + face roles + original->flat map). On failure, the ok:false branch still carries the partial diagnostics gathered before the failure.

kind.description: 'cyl' and 'cone' fold through a bend face of that surface; 'sharp' folds along a shared edge with no bend face (faceIndex -1, inner radius 0), and a 0 degree 'sharp' fold joins two coplanar panels.

UnfoldBend.description: One bend: line, angle, radii (inner/outer/neutral and per-end for cones), and developed lengths.

tangentDot.description: Bend candidates (cylinder/cone) only: best |flange normal · cylinder radial| over the flanges. ~1 = tangent fold, ~0 = cutout/hole wall.

bendOutcome.description: How the fold filter classified a bend candidate: 'fold' (kept), 'cutout' (rejected - not tangent / <2 flanges), 'duplicate' (dropped - one fold per flat pair), or '' (a bend face not on the reference side, never evaluated by the filter).

UnfoldFaceEntry.description: A classified source face: stable key (index + BRepGraph uid), role, and label anchors.

UnfoldPlaced.description: A sub-shape laid into the flat compound, mapped back to its source face (compound order).

UnfoldSolidReportError.description: Returned when a solid cannot be fully unfolded; carries the partial diagnostics gathered before the failure (classified faces with roles, detected thickness, warnings) so the reason can be inspected.

stock.description: The index of the stock in the options' sheets.

width.description: The sheet's width; for a strip, the length it used.

origin.description: Where the sheet's corner lies in the working space, Y up, the sheet on the XZ plane facing +Y. A STEP output turns this space to Z up.

NestingSheetEntry.description: One used sheet: its stock, where it lies in the working space, and how much of it the parts fill.

box.description: The part's box on its sheet as [minX, minY, maxX, maxY].

anchor.description: A point inside the placed part's material, for a label, in the working space (Y up).

transform.description: The 4 x 4 matrix, column by column, that moves the input part to its place in the working space (Y up); a STEP output is that space turned to Z up.

NestingPlacement.description: Where one copy of a part was placed.

file.description: Which uploaded file the part came from, as an index into stepFileIds; present on the nesting routes, which read parts from files.

solid.description: Which solid of the model the flat pattern was unfolded from, as its solidIndex in the unfold report; present on the unfold-and-nest route.

problem.description: Why the part cannot be nested: nullShape, notPlanar, notClosed, notPlate, unsupportedShape or invalidGeometry.

kind.description: What the part was read as: face, faces, solid, wire or wires.

depth.description: A plate's thickness; 0 for a face or a drawing.

slack.description: How far the outline's chords may stray from the true edges; added to the spacing.

NestingPartEntry.description: How one part was read, and how many of its copies were placed.

reason.description: The part's problem, or tooLargeForAnySheet, noStockLeft, timeBudget or verificationFailed.

NestingLeft.description: Copies of a part that were not placed, and why.

NestingRun.description: How the search ran: whether the same seed gives the same layout again, and whether it was stopped or ran out of time.

NestingReportError.description: The nesting kernel's own answer when it refuses the options or is stopped before any part was nested. No result carries it: the API fails the task with its error instead.

circle.description: The centre's x and y and the radius.

points.description: The vertices as x, y pairs, one after another.

bulges.description: One per vertex: the tangent of a quarter of the arc's angle from that vertex to the next, 0 for a straight line, positive turning counterclockwise.

NestingOutlinePolyline.description: Lines and arcs from vertex to vertex.

majorAxis.description: The vector from the centre to one end of the major axis; its length is the major radius.

ratio.description: The minor radius divided by the major radius.

start.description: Where the arc starts, as the ellipse's parameter t in radians: the point center + cos(t) majorAxis + sin(t) ratio (-majorAxis y, majorAxis x), the minor axis being the major one turned a quarter counterclockwise and scaled by ratio. t is the angle from the major axis only when ratio is 1.

end.description: Where the arc ends, as the same parameter t in radians; the arc runs counterclockwise from start to end, a whole ellipse from 0 to 2 pi.

NestingOutlineEllipse.description: An ellipse or an arc of one.

knots.description: The full knot vector, one more value than the control points and the degree together; the curve starts and ends at its end points.

points.description: The control points as x, y pairs, one after another.

weights.description: One weight per control point when the curve is rational; left out, every weight is 1.

NestingSheetEntryOutput.description: One used sheet: its stock, where it lies in the working space, and how much of it the parts fill.

box.description: The part's box on its sheet as [minX, minY, maxX, maxY].

anchor.description: A point inside the placed part's material, for a label, in the working space (Y up).

transform.description: The 4 x 4 matrix, column by column, that moves the input part to its place in the working space (Y up); a STEP output is that space turned to Z up.

NestingPlacementOutput.description: Where one copy of a part was placed.

file.description: Which uploaded file the part came from, as an index into stepFileIds; present on the nesting routes, which read parts from files.

solid.description: Which solid of the model the flat pattern was unfolded from, as its solidIndex in the unfold report; present on the unfold-and-nest route.

problem.description: Why the part cannot be nested: nullShape, notPlanar, notClosed, notPlate, unsupportedShape or invalidGeometry.

kind.description: What the part was read as: face, faces, solid, wire or wires.

depth.description: A plate's thickness; 0 for a face or a drawing.

slack.description: How far the outline's chords may stray from the true edges; added to the spacing.

NestingPartEntryOutput.description: How one part was read, and how many of its copies were placed.

reason.description: The part's problem, or tooLargeForAnySheet, noStockLeft, timeBudget or verificationFailed.

NestingLeftOutput.description: Copies of a part that were not placed, and why.

NestingRunOutput.description: How the search ran: whether the same seed gives the same layout again, and whether it was stopped or ran out of time.

NestingReportErrorOutput.description: The nesting kernel's own answer when it refuses the options or is stopped before any part was nested. No result carries it: the API fails the task with its error instead.

circle.description: The centre's x and y and the radius.

points.description: The vertices as x, y pairs, one after another.

bulges.description: One per vertex: the tangent of a quarter of the arc's angle from that vertex to the next, 0 for a straight line, positive turning counterclockwise.

NestingOutlinePolylineOutput.description: Lines and arcs from vertex to vertex.

majorAxis.description: The vector from the centre to one end of the major axis; its length is the major radius.

ratio.description: The minor radius divided by the major radius.

start.description: Where the arc starts, as the ellipse's parameter t in radians: the point center + cos(t) majorAxis + sin(t) ratio (-majorAxis y, majorAxis x), the minor axis being the major one turned a quarter counterclockwise and scaled by ratio. t is the angle from the major axis only when ratio is 1.

end.description: Where the arc ends, as the same parameter t in radians; the arc runs counterclockwise from start to end, a whole ellipse from 0 to 2 pi.

NestingOutlineEllipseOutput.description: An ellipse or an arc of one.

knots.description: The full knot vector, one more value than the control points and the degree together; the curve starts and ends at its end points.

points.description: The control points as x, y pairs, one after another.

weights.description: One weight per control point when the curve is rational; left out, every weight is 1.

UnfoldFaceReport.description: Sheet-metal unfold metrics for a single face (surface type, developability, area before/after).

UnfoldSolidReport.description: Per-solid sheet-metal unfold metrics - one entry per solid in the STEP file (each carries its solidIndex).

NestingReport.description: The layout of a nesting run: the used sheets, every placement with its transform, each part as read, what was left and why, and the totals. Every length is in the parts' units, millimetres for parts read from STEP files. Positions are in the working space, right-handed with Y up; a STEP output turns that space to Z up, a quarter turn about X. A report delivered as a result always has ok true: when the kernel refuses a run, the task fails with the kernel's reason instead.

NestingInspection.description: Each part as nesting reads it, without nesting. Every length is in the parts' units, millimetres for parts read from STEP files. A report delivered as a result always has ok true: when the kernel refuses a run, the task fails with the kernel's reason instead.

placement.description: The placement in the report this copy is.

path.description: The same cut path as SVG path data in the sheet's frame, y up: arcs and ellipses exact, splines as Bezier curves.

NestingOutlines.description: The cut paths of every placed copy in the frame of its sheet: x along the sheet's width and y along its height from the corner, as the report's placement boxes are; the 'outlines' result of a nest.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Scoped API key. Scopes: models, cad, convert, * (wildcard). A key without the required scope receives 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE.
